hub.title: Meme Encyclopedia: Meanings, Origins and Trends of Viral Memes
hub.description: What is Tung Tung Tung Sahur, Chill Guy, Pepe, aura or 6 7? {n} viral memes and internet slang explained: what they mean, where and when they started, and how popular they are now.
hub.lede: Viral memes and internet slang, one page each: what it is, where and when it started, how people use it, and whether it is still rising. Italian brainrot, classic memes, viral animals, Gen Alpha slang and Chinese internet memes.

groups.gen-alpha: Gen Z and Gen Alpha slang

about: Every entry answers the question first, then gives a dated timeline of where the meme came from and how it spread, shows how people use it, and says where it stands now.

Memes are picked from what people actually search for, and facts are checked against Wikipedia, Know Your Meme, dictionaries and news reports. Popularity curves come from Wikipedia page views and refresh daily.

faq.a: An image, video, sound, phrase or character that people copy, remix and pass on online, such as Pepe the Frog, Rickroll or Tung Tung Tung Sahur. The word was coined by Richard Dawkins in 1976 for any idea that spreads from person to person.
A 2025 wave of AI-generated absurd characters with fake-Italian names and text-to-speech voices, such as Tralalero Tralala and Tung Tung Tung Sahur, that spread on TikTok. Each has its own page here.

faq.q: Why do some memes have crypto tokens?
faq.a: Anyone can create a token and name it after a famous meme, so most viral memes get one. They are not made by the meme's creator unless stated, and their prices are extremely volatile.
